answer: Cross-time consistency audits resist sybils: at unpredictable moments, each agent must complete a task that only fits its own history, from the dawn of its first job to its latest work. A genuine record cannot be cloned across many identities, because every audit is personalized and time-windowed, like a single wharf that serves one ship at a time rather than a jetty crowded with identical boats. An attacker with many fakes must maintain a separate history for each and answer every surprise check on time, so cost rises with each added identity, while one honest agent pays almost nothing.
